pydantic::pydantic/types.py::_check_anno: Checks that the type being annotated matches the expected type. Raises an error if they differ.
pydantic::pydantic/types.py::_get_type_n: Returns a short name for the type of a value, such as int, str, list or dict. Subclasses are reported as their basic type.
pydantic::pydantic/types.py::condecimal: Creates an exact-decimal number type with limits such as maximum digits or decimal places.
pydantic::pydantic/types.py::confloat: Creates a decimal-number type with limits (for example between 0 and 1). Older style; Annotated with Field is now preferred.
pydantic::pydantic/types.py::conint: Creates a whole-number type with limits (for example greater than 0, or a multiple of 5). Older style; Annotated with Field is now preferred.
pydantic::pydantic/types.py::constr: Creates a text type with rules such as minimum/maximum length, a pattern, or turning the text to upper or lower case.
pydantic::pydantic/validate_call_decorat: Wraps a function so that its inputs (and optionally its result) are checked against the function's type hints every time it is called.
pydantic::pydantic/version.py::_ensure_p: Checks that the installed pydantic-core version matches what Pydantic needs. Raises an error if it does not, unless Pydantic runs in development mode.
requests::requests/__init__.py::_check_c: Checks a cryptography version text and shows a warning if the version is older than 1.3.4. It does nothing if the version cannot be read as numbers.
requests::requests/hooks.py::default_hoo: Returns a new dictionary with an empty list for each known hook event name.
requests::requests/status_codes.py::_ini: Sets up the table of status codes. For each code and name it adds attributes to the codes object and builds the documentation text.
requests::requests/utils.py::_validate_h: Checks that a header name or value is valid and has a proper type, string or bytes. Raises an error if it is not valid.
requests::requests/utils.py::default_hea: Returns the default HTTP headers as a case-insensitive dictionary, including user agent, accepted encodings, accept and connection values.
requests::requests/utils.py::is_ipv4_add: Checks whether a text is a valid IPv4 address. Returns True or False.
requests::requests/utils.py::super_len: Works out the length in bytes of an object such as a string, bytes or file, taking the current read position into account. Returns the remaining length as a number.
rich::rich/_extension.py::load_ipython_e: Sets up Rich pretty printing and nicer error tracebacks in an IPython notebook session.
rich::rich/console.py::detect_legacy_win: Checks whether the program runs on an old Windows console that lacks modern terminal support. Returns True or False.
rich::rich/console.py::get_windows_conso: Returns the Windows console feature information, finding it once and remembering it for later calls.
rich::rich/control.py::Control.bell: Creates a control code that makes the terminal ring its bell. Returns a Control object.
rich::rich/control.py::Control.show_curs: Creates a control code that shows or hides the cursor, depending on the given True or False value. Returns a Control object.
rich::rich/filesize.py::_to_str: Turns a size in bytes into readable text such as 1.5 MB, using the given unit names, base, number of decimals and separator. Returns the text.
rich::rich/jupyter.py::_render_segments: Turns styled text pieces into an HTML string for display in a notebook, escaping special characters and skipping control pieces. Returns the HTML text.
rich::rich/jupyter.py::print: Prints the given values using the shared Rich console. It passes all arguments on and returns nothing.
rich::rich/pretty.py::_ipy_display_hook: Display helper for IPython that shows a value as nicely formatted text with Rich. It skips values that Rich already made and returns text or None.
rich::rich/repr.py::rich_repr: Describes a function that marks a class so Rich can show it nicely. This is only a type signature with no real code.
rich::rich/segment.py::Segment.line: Creates and returns a segment of text that is just a new line.
rich::rich/traceback.py::Traceback._gues: Guesses which programming language a piece of code is, from the file extension or the first line. Returns the language name used for highlighting.
